prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key commitments and measures (max 500 words)

Economy, business and work
- Repair EU trading relations; responsible fiscal rules; expand British Business Bank.
- Green-led growth: large-scale investment in renewables, insulation and skills.
- Tax changes: reverse bank tax cuts; one-off windfall tax on oil/gas; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; fairer capital gains; 4% levy on FTSE-100 share buybacks.
- Replace apprenticeship levy with flexible skills levy; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants (aim £10,000).
- Reform business rates to a Commercial Landowner Levy; late payments crackdown.
- Modernise employment rights: new “dependent contractor” status; fair SSP from day one and at least minimum wage level; zero-hour protections; independent Worker Protection Authority; living wage review.
- AI framework focusing on safety, transparency and innovation; Horizon Europe participation; R&D to 3–3.5% of GDP.

Climate, energy and environment
- Net zero by 2045; 90% electricity from renewables by 2030.
- Ten-year home energy upgrade (free for low-income), zero‑carbon new homes, social energy tariff, decouple electricity from gas prices.
- Remove barriers to onshore wind/solar; ban fracking and new coal; expand storage and interconnectors; empower community energy.
- Corporate climate duties; UK ETS–EU ETS linkage; industrial decarbonisation support and CBAM.
- End sewage discharges: tougher regulator, sewage tax, targets for bathing waters; transform water firms to public benefit companies.
- “Double nature” by 2050; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act; deposit return scheme; phase-out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; peat and blue‑carbon restoration; protect 30% of land/sea by 2030.

Health and care
- GP access right: within 7 days (24 hours urgent); +8,000 GPs; pharmacy/nurse prescribing; universal 24/7 booking; rural surgeries fund.
- NHS dentistry access; supervised toothbrushing; targeted exemptions.
- Mental health: walk‑in hubs for youth; regular check‑ups at life stages; specialist in every school; end out‑of‑area placements.
- Cancer: 62‑day treatment guarantee; more radiotherapy machines; more cancer nurses; faster approvals.
- Public health measures on tobacco, vapes, sugar; air quality action.
- Ten‑year estates plan; patient charter; digital interoperability; virtual wards.
- Drugs policy public‑health led; legal, regulated cannabis market.
- Social care: free personal care; workforce plan; Royal College of Care Workers; carers’ minimum wage (+£2/h), paid leave and respite; National Care Agency; portability of care packages; kinship care support.

Education and families
- Mental health professional in every school; per‑pupil funding above inflation; tutoring guarantee; repair crumbling buildings.
- Early years: extra free hours for disadvantaged 3–4s; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Restore maintenance grants; SEND funding reform and national body; Ofsted reform.
- Parental leave/pay: day‑one rights incl self‑employed; double Statutory Maternity/Shared Parental Pay (£350/wk); enhanced paternity; paid neonatal leave.
- Free school meals for all children in poverty; Erasmus+ return.

Housing and communities
- 380,000 homes/year (150,000 social); 10 garden cities; councils buy land at current use value; brownfield with affordable quotas; “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it” permissions; zero‑carbon standards.
- Renters: end Section 21; default three‑year tenancies; national landlord register.
- Abolish residential leasehold; cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding at no leaseholder cost; Rent‑to‑Own for social housing.
- End rough sleeping; scrap Vagrancy Act; local powers over second homes/short lets; gigabit broadband nationwide.

Transport
- Accelerate EV rollout: more chargers, 5% VAT on public charging, card access, restore plug‑in grant; 2030 ZEV mandate.
- Freeze rail fares; new Railway Agency; electrification, Northern Powerhouse Rail; accessibility; bus franchising and £2 cap; active travel; more road‑maintenance funding.
- Aviation: tax frequent/private jet flying more; show emissions vs rail; ban short domestic flights where rail <2.5h; moratorium on airport expansion.

Rights, policing and justice
- Community policing; guarantee police attendance for burglaries; Online Crime Agency; cut court backlogs; youth diversion; fraud protections.
- Uphold Human Rights Act and ECHR; Digital Bill of Rights; regulate biometrics; strengthen VAWG support; protect reproductive healthcare access; equality reporting; disability employment support; assisted dying free vote.

Immigration and asylum
- Move work/student visa policy out of Home Office; flexible, sector‑led work visa criteria; reverse family visa threshold rises; expand Youth Mobility.
- Scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; 3‑month asylum decision standard; allow work after 3 months; safe/legal routes (resettlement, humanitarian permits, family reunion); implement Windrush review; EU citizens automatic Settled Status with physical proof.

Political reform and international
- Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; scrap voter ID; votes at 16; cap donations; Lords reform; federal constitution; transparency on lobbying and ministerial communications.
- Defence: grow Army over time; spend towards 2.5% GDP; maintain deterrent; procurement reform; stronger European/NATO cooperation.
- Foreign policy: rebuild EU ties via staged roadmap (including Single Market aim); support Ukraine incl using seized Russian assets; restore 0.7% ODA with independent department; ceasefire and two‑state track for Israel–Palestine; targeted human‑rights sanctions; BBC World Service funding.
